author: LegalEagle
description:
A Trump pardon could wipe out Pete Hegseth’s federal criminal exposure, but there’s one thing it can’t touch 📜

The legal questions trace back to the September 2 boat strikes. The Washington Post reported that Hegseth gave a verbal order to kill everybody. Admiral Frank Bradley told lawmakers there was no such order, and Hegseth says he watched the first strike, left, and didn’t learn about the second until hours later. Who said what, and when, is exactly what a future grand jury would want to know.

We don’t know whether a future DOJ would ever bring charges, but the timelines matter. Federal law sets no statute of limitations for crimes punishable by death, including first-degree federal murder and war crimes that result in death. Lesser charges like second-degree murder and conspiracy fall under the general five-year limit, which for the September 2 strikes runs out in September 2030. title: The One Thing a Trump Pardon Can’t Stop for Hegseth
